svg.title: Quantization: a sensor counts in steps
svg.desc: Animated. A dial marked with the 42 counts per turn of a NEO's built-in sensor: a thin gray needle turns smoothly, the true angle, while the orange needle, what the sensor reads, jumps from one count mark to the next. Beside it, the angle graph draws a smooth gray curve and an orange staircase of whole counts, one count per step. Below, the speed worked out from the counts jumps between zero and spikes while the true speed is a smooth hump. Through the 46.42:1 steering gearbox one count is about 0.18 degrees of module angle: fine for position. For speed it is coarse, so the SPARK averages, which adds delay. A high kP times a jumpy measurement makes a buzz.
svg.text: Quantization: a sensor counts in steps
A NEO's built-in sensor has 42 counts per turn, so small moves and speeds look jumpy.
Angle: the reading moves in steps
Speed worked out from the counts: jumpy
Fine for position: through the 46.42:1 gearbox, one count is about 0.18°.
Coarse for speed, so the SPARK averages, which adds delay.
A high kP times a jumpy measurement makes a buzz.
